list.title: Tier 1 (e.g., preferred generics):
list.snippet: Usually the lowest cost-sharing tier, often including generic drugs.

list.title: Tier 2 (e.g., preferred brand-name drugs):
list.snippet: These are typically brand-name medications that have a lower cost-sharing amount than drugs in higher tiers. They may or may not have generic equivalents.

list.title: Tier 3 (e.g., non-preferred brand-name drugs):
list.snippet: These are brand-name drugs that are generally more expensive than those in Tier 2 and may have generic or brand-name alternatives available at a lower cost, according to Oscar.

list.title: Tier 4 (e.g., specialty drugs):
list.snippet: The highest cost tier, often reserved for specialty medications used to treat complex or serious illnesses.

text_blocks.snippet: In essence, tier 2 medications represent a middle ground in terms of cost and availability compared to other medication tiers.
